title: Biomarker for injury-associated pneumonias
summary: After serious accidents, many patients suffer severe chest injuries. These can take various forms, such as multiple broken ribs breaking at multiple points in the chest. Such injuries can lead to breathing problems and often require intensive medical treatment, including possible surgeries and long-term ventilation. In our study, we are investigating whether early surgery within 72 hours of the accident can help reduce ventilation time and other complications in these injuries. We also want to explore how this treatment affects the patients' immune systems and whether specific blood markers can help predict complications such as pneumonia. The findings could help improve the treatment of chest injuries and support patient recovery.

interventions.name: Osteosynthesis of unstable thoracic injury within 72 hours after the accident, followed by inpatient therapy according to current internal clinical standards.
Conservative inpatient therapy according to current internal clinical standards.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Adult patients ≥ 18 years old
2) Radiological evidence of an unstable thorax, defined as:
2.1) ≥ 3 consecutive ribs, each with a segmental fracture (≥ 2 fracture sites)
3) Possibility of surgical intervention within 72 hours of admission
Exclusion criteria:
1) Comorbidities or additional injuries that preclude surgical intervention within the aforementioned timeframe
